tb21_profile.skill: Write a single dependency-free C file, under a hard byte budget, that parses an undocumented binary weight file plus a BPE merge table and reimplements a published model's forward pass numerically correctly
tb21_profile.domain: Transformer/LLM internals (attention, layernorm, GELU, argmax decoding), BPE tokenisation, TensorFlow checkpoint binary layout, plain C with only libm
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec under a size budget, graded on exact generated output

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. software-engineering_20260601_053159_010 (dependency-free C Huffman codec) belongs to the same CalibForge template family but is graded FREE, so I left it out of per_source rather than rank an unverifiable member of an otherwise strong family.
searches: tools.py search all '(?i)code ?golf|fewest (bytes|characters)|under \d+ bytes|byte limit|smallest possible (program|binary)'
tools.py search tmax '(?i)neural network|from scratch (in|using) c|matrix multiplication|inference (engine|in c)|numpy-free|without (numpy|any libraries)|forward pass'
tools.py search tmax '(?i)\.ckpt|checkpoint file|model weights|float32 .{0,30}binary|little-endian float'
tools.py search tw '(?i)write a c (program|file)|implement.{0,30}(in c|from scratch)|assembly program|parse.{0,20}(binary|elf|format)|float'
tools.py search rts '(?i)write a c (program|file)|implement .{0,30}(algorithm|from scratch)|compile .{0,20}with gcc'

TMax-15K.reason: C program that reads model weights off disk and scores cleaned data; a C inference path driven by a weights file, strongly verified.
Build the C tokenizer that feeds a custom C LLM inference engine, and benchmark it; tokenisation in C for exactly this pipeline.
Load a weight matrix and bias vector and implement ReLU(XW+b) by hand; the matmul-plus-nonlinearity core of a forward pass.
Reproduce a lost binary's float32 output exactly, writing the same little-endian layout; byte-exact numerical reimplementation.
Match an oracle's binary output byte for byte - magic header then packed 32-bit little-endian floats - under fuzz comparison.
Implement a Metropolis-Hastings sampler from scratch in C over a CSV; numerically correct algorithm in plain C, strong verifier.
Read weights from a file and chain matrix multiplications to a scalar score; small but the same weights-to-prediction arithmetic.
Implement KNN from scratch in C with cross-validation and a specified tie-break; algorithm-from-description in C.
Train a byte-pair-encoding tokenizer from scratch; BPE merge semantics, which the C program must apply at inference time.
Recreate a lost script from recovered .npz weights - infer the architecture from the weight tensors alone, as reading a ckpt requires.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Write a decoder for 7-bit binary lines with a configurable offset and a CLI; bit-level decoding into text, small but real.
C program using clone(CLONE_NEWPID) and reboot() that must adapt to the running kernel; genuine low-level C, not boilerplate.
C program with a precise fork/exec/wait output protocol; exact stdout from hand-written C.
C program whose output must match a reference file exactly, with no trailing newline - byte-exact output discipline.
Second clone/reboot variant; same systems-C skill, slightly different verification story.
Set up and run an MNIST similarity tool that renders digits; touches model inference but only as a user of the tool.
Run an image-similarity classifier, fixing the script until it works; ML domain, debugging rather than implementation.
Compile and run a numeric C program and match a reference output exactly; float formatting matters, nothing else does.
C program that must pick up a value at build time; build plumbing, essentially the corpus's num: 599 boilerplate.
Multi-file C program built through a provided build system; included to fill the quota, transfers almost nothing.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Demonstrate exact accumulation against IEEE float error on linear systems; the numerical-precision reasoning an argmax forward pass needs. Strong verifier.
Perform a series of fixed-point and floating-point conversions with exact expected values; number-representation work.
Hand-write an assembly program against a simulator's instruction set to produce a required machine state; low-level exactness.
Feed prefix expressions to an evaluator and capture exact output including the error case; parse-and-evaluate with pinned results.
ARM64 assembly that rewrites a string byte by byte; manual buffer manipulation with an exactly specified output.
ARM64 assembly producing the first ten Fibonacci numbers; loop and output formatting at the instruction level.
Compile and run a C program that prints square roots in a fixed format; libm plus exact output formatting, nothing more.
Train a model on a split and emit predictions to a file; model inference domain, driven entirely by an existing tool.
Compute cosine similarity between word vectors from two models; embedding arithmetic, but library-driven.
Write and compile a trivial C program printing a fixed integer; quota filler.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: A loss formula transcribed with operands swapped returns the wrong number; getting a published formula exactly right is this task's core risk.
smooth_l1_loss produces completely wrong values; debugging a numerical kernel against known expected outputs.
FLOP counting for matmul is broken; reasoning about matrix-multiply shapes and cost, the dominant op in a transformer.
Running mean and variance accumulate incorrectly; the same running-statistics arithmetic layernorm depends on.
Tensor-to-array conversion mishandles certain shapes; dimension bookkeeping, which flat C arrays make even easier to get wrong.
A squeeze-excitation module's forward pass fails on valid input; module-level forward correctness in a neural network.
Bit-packed frame encoding and verification over raw bytes; the bit-and-byte layout discipline reading a checkpoint demands.
LZW decoder produces wrong bytes; stateful decoding of a packed binary stream with an exact expected result.
Floats parsed as ints and vice versa; numeric literal handling, relevant only to careful float parsing.
Token processing returns empty results; tokenisation bookkeeping, far shallower than BPE merges.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Writing a binary file format produces an invalid file when byteorder is big and strings use the long form; endianness and layout correctness.
A binary-template interpreter that parses arbitrary file formats by declared struct layout - the ckpt-reading skill, in Python.
Seeding the language-modeling data collator; same library and model family, but the fix is plumbing rather than architecture.
Generate correct C for a new return type, including its memory handling; writing C that must compile and behave exactly.
Rotation-and-XOR over bit vectors has a provable degeneracy; bit-level maths reasoning of the kind tight C encodings need.
Extend a serialiser's handling of a type across its binary and JSON encodings; wire-format design and exactness.
Follow-up on collator seeding in the same library; GPT-2-era transformer ecosystem, shallow change.
Generating subnormal floats correctly; forces precise reasoning about IEEE-754 representation, which C float code needs.
Crash in the C code printer; debugging a tool that emits C, adjacent to writing C by hand.
An exotic raster dtype breaks chunking; typed binary buffers, but the fix is dtype plumbing.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Portable buffer-to-struct interpretation in C: alignment, aliasing and layout when reading records out of a byte buffer - exactly ckpt reading.
Serialise and deserialise floats across endiannesses; float32 byte order is the first thing a hand-written ckpt reader gets wrong.
Implement word2vec skip-gram with negative sampling from its description; building a published model's maths from the paper, strongly verified.
Disk-based B-tree library in C: design an on-disk binary layout and read it back through file I/O with no libraries.
Implement convolution filters from first principles rather than calling a framework; array-index arithmetic for a neural op.
Softmax versus softmax-cross-entropy, including the numerical-stability difference; the exact op before argmax sampling.
Marshal a struct out of a raw byte array; the same reinterpret-these-bytes-as-fields step, in a managed language.
Find duplicates in a large dataset under a memory ceiling; designing to a hard resource budget, like the 5000-byte limit.
Disk-backed container in C++: keep a data structure on disk and page it in; storage layout thinking, heavier machinery.
Binary tree rendering in C with exact expected output; plain-C buffer and formatting work, no numerics.

Write a C inference engine for a trained model whose weights come from a saved data file; the ML-in-C half, strongly verified.
Self-contained C that reads the raw SQLite v3 file format with no library; parsing a complex undocumented container by hand, as with a ckpt.
Dependency-free C under 1500 bytes producing a byte-correct archive; the tightest size budget in the pool.
tar extractor in one C file under 3000 bytes supporting USTAR and PAX; format variants plus a byte budget at once.
DEFLATE decompressor in dependency-free C handling all three block types; bit-stream decoding implemented from the specification.
gzip compressor in C under 4000 bytes producing output other tools must accept; same budgeted single-file discipline.
Single-file C PNG decoder emitting exact RGBA bytes; chunk parsing, zlib inflate and filters, all by hand.
A custom transformer encoder with embeddings, positional encoding and attention layers to get right; the architecture this task must reimplement.
A tiny GPT-2 checkpoint whose config and weights will not load; forces understanding how the weights map onto the architecture.

final_top10.reason: Dependency-free C binary-format decoder at /app, gcc -O3 -lm, under 5000 bytes - the same instruction template, same constraints.
Write a C inference engine that loads a trained model's saved weights and reproduces its predictions; the ML-in-C half exactly.
Parse the raw SQLite v3 file format in self-contained C; reverse-reading a complex on-disk container with no library, like a .ckpt.
C program that reads model weights from a file and runs inference over input data; weights-file-to-prediction in plain C.
Dependency-free C under 1500 bytes that must still emit a byte-correct format; the strictest code-golf budget available.
Build the C tokenizer feeding a custom C LLM inference engine - tokenisation in C for precisely this kind of program.
Portable reinterpretation of a byte buffer as structured fields in C: alignment and aliasing, the first hazard in reading a ckpt.
Implement DEFLATE decoding in C straight from the specification, all block types; spec-to-correct-bit-stream-code in one file.
Get a transformer encoder's embeddings, positional encoding and attention stack correct; the architecture this task reimplements in C.
Implement skip-gram with negative sampling from its description; building a published model's maths from a written spec.

notes: CalibForge is decisive here and for an unusual reason: it contains a whole authored family built on the same instruction template as this TB2.1 task - 'write me a dependency-free C file at /app/X.c, I will compile with gcc -O3 -lm, it must be under N bytes' - applied to PNG, gzip, DEFLATE, tar, ar and the SQLite file format, almost all graded strong. Nothing in the v1 pool has that shape. Add its C-inference-engine and transformer-encoder tasks and CalibForge supplies the binary-parsing, size-budget and model-architecture axes separately; no single task in any corpus combines all three the way gpt2-codegolf does. TMax is a real second: its C-inference-from-a-weights-file and C-tokenizer tasks are the only v1 entries that put ML numerics in C. Terminal-Lego is better than its shortlist suggests - retrieval returned nothing useful, but its own search surfaces byte-buffer/endianness C tasks and a from-the-paper word2vec implementation, mostly strongly verified. Recursive-Task-Synthesis genuinely cannot field 10 defensible candidates: its C content is the repeated 'print num: 599' build exercise, so ranks 6-10 there are near-worthless and should not be selected. TerminalWorld is also thin - its best offering is float-precision and hand-written assembly, nothing ML. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench are ranked on numerics and binary-format domain only; the fvcore cluster is the most defensible SWE-Smith block because those bugs are wrong formulas and wrong shapes, which is the failure mode of a hand-written forward pass.
